title: Breaking Bad
note: Written by Claude for Watch Together. Moments are approximate (fraction of the runtime, in scene order).

items.fact: Vince Gilligan first set the show in Riverside, California; it moved to Albuquerque, New Mexico, because of the state's filming incentives.
Gilligan cast Bryan Cranston after working with him on 'Drive', an episode of The X-Files - the network had wanted a bigger star.
Before this, Cranston was best known as the goofy dad Hal in 'Malcolm in the Middle'.
Gilligan pitched the show as turning 'Mr. Chips into Scarface'.

entries.title: Breaking Bad – Cat's in the Bag... (S1E2)

items.fact: The bathtub scene was later tested on MythBusters - they found hydrofluoric acid would not eat through a tub and floor like that.

names: and the bags in the river
entries.title: Breaking Bad – ...And the Bag's in the River (S1E3)

items.fact: Walt's pros-and-cons list about killing Krazy-8 is one of the show's early signs of who Walt will become.
Aaron Paul's character was originally meant to die at the end of Season 1; Gilligan changed his mind after seeing Paul's work.
Gray Matter Technologies - the company Walt co-founded and left - is the root of his resentment toward Elliott and Gretchen.

entries.title: Breaking Bad – Crazy Handful of Nothin' (S1E6)

items.fact: Walt's alias 'Heisenberg' refers to physicist Werner Heisenberg, known for the uncertainty principle.
MythBusters later tested the 'fulminated mercury' explosion and found it couldn't be thrown like that without going off.

names: a no rough stuff type deal
entries.title: Breaking Bad – A No-Rough-Stuff-Type Deal (S1E7)

items.fact: Season 1 had only seven episodes because of the 2007–08 Writers Guild strike.
The titles of four Season 2 episodes - 'Seven Thirty-Seven', 'Down', 'Over', 'ABQ' - form a hidden sentence that foreshadows the season finale.
Mark Margolis plays Hector 'Tio' Salamanca, who communicates only with a bell - he later reprised the role in Better Call Saul.

entries.title: Breaking Bad – Bit by a Dead Bee (S2E3)

items.fact: Walt fakes a 'fugue state' to explain his disappearance - one of his first big lies to his family.
'Down' is the second word of the hidden Season 2 sentence: Seven Thirty-Seven / Down / Over / ABQ.
Hank's anxiety after the shootout is one of the first looks at Dean Norris's dramatic range in the role.
Many critics call Aaron Paul's scenes with the little boy in this episode his breakout performance.
The opening music video is a real narcocorrido by Los Cuates de Sinaloa written for the show, about the legend of Heisenberg.
Bob Odenkirk's Saul Goodman was planned as a small role - he later got his own prequel series, 'Better Call Saul'.
'Saul Goodman' is a play on 'S'all good, man'.
Walt builds a battery from scraps when the RV dies in the desert - the episode was mostly shot with just two actors.
'Over' is the third word of the hidden Season 2 sentence.
Gus Fring makes his first appearance here - Giancarlo Esposito later reprised the role in Better Call Saul.
Jane's father Donald is played by John de Lancie - Q from Star Trek: The Next Generation.
'ABQ' completes the hidden sentence: 'Seven thirty-seven down over ABQ' - the season's mid-air collision.
The Cousins are played by real-life brothers Luis and Daniel Moncada.
The episode title means 'Horse with No Name' - Walt sings along to the America song in the car.
Skyler's three words to Walt give the episode its abbreviated title.
Skyler's affair with her boss Ted Beneke drives much of Season 3's family drama.
The superlab set under the laundromat was one of the show's biggest builds.
Hank finally corners the RV in a junkyard - the end of the show's most famous vehicle.
Hank's parking-lot shootout with the Cousins is considered one of the show's best action sequences.
Gus's hospital visit is a turning point: the first time Walt sees how far Gus's reach goes.
Jesse's 'Kafkaesque' description of the lab is a callback to his support-group sessions.
'Fly' was directed by Rian Johnson, who later made 'Star Wars: The Last Jedi' and 'Knives Out'.
It's a 'bottle episode' set almost entirely in the lab - made partly to save money, now one of the most debated episodes.
Abiquiú is the New Mexico town where painter Georgia O'Keeffe lived - Jane's favourite artist.
Jonathan Banks's 'no more half measures' monologue is one of Mike Ehrmantraut's best-known scenes.
Gale Boetticher is played by David Costabile; Gilligan left the ending's outcome ambiguous for the whole summer break.
Giancarlo Esposito's wordless scene with the box cutter is often named the moment Gus became one of TV's great villains.
A '.38 snub' is a short-barrelled revolver - Walt buys it to deal with Gus.
Marie's habit of stealing from open houses under fake names is a running thread of her kleptomania.
Gale's karaoke video is set to 'Major Tom (Coming Home)' by Peter Schilling.
'I am the one who knocks' - Walt's speech to Skyler became one of the show's signature lines.
Jesse's veiled 'problem dog' story in group therapy gives the episode its name.
The flashback reveals Gus's past with his partner Max and why 'Los Pollos Hermanos' means 'the chicken brothers'.
The overhead shot of Walt laughing in the crawl space is one of the most iconic images of the series.
The famous reveal was created with prosthetic make-up combined with digital effects.
The last shot shows a Lily of the Valley plant - the answer to the season's mystery.

entries.title: Breaking Bad – Live Free or Die (S5E1)

items.fact: The flash-forward to Walt's 52nd birthday at a Denny's set up the final season's mystery.
Madrigal Electromotive, a German conglomerate, owns Los Pollos Hermanos; Laura Fraser joins as Lydia.
Walt Jr. watches 'Scarface' with Walt - a nod to Gilligan's 'Mr. Chips to Scarface' pitch.
Anna Gunn's pool scene on Walt's 51st birthday is one of her most praised performances; she won two Emmys for the role.
The deeply awkward dinner with Walt, Skyler and Jesse is often called the show's funniest dark scene.
'Say my name.' 'Heisenberg.' 'You're goddamn right.' - one of the most quoted exchanges in TV history.
The prison montage is set to Nat King Cole's 'Pick Yourself Up'.
The book Hank picks up is Walt Whitman's 'Leaves of Grass', inscribed by Gale.
The final eight episodes aired in 2013 and drew the series' biggest audiences.
The desert burial location becomes crucial to the series' last episodes.
Walt's 'confession' video is one of the most chilling things he does in the series.
The episode leaves Jesse with Hank and Marie - an alliance fans never expected.
To'hajiilee is a real Navajo community in New Mexico - near where Walt and Jesse cooked their very first batch.
Directed by Rian Johnson; it is often ranked as the greatest TV episode ever made and was rated 10/10 on IMDb.
The title is Percy Shelley's sonnet about a fallen king; Bryan Cranston recited it in a teaser for the final season.
Robert Forster plays Ed, the vacuum-repair man who 'disappears' people; he returned in the film 'El Camino'.
'Granite State' is New Hampshire's nickname.
'Felina' is an anagram of 'finale' and a nod to Feleena in Marty Robbins' song 'El Paso', which Walt hums.
The final scene plays Badfinger's 'Baby Blue' - Walt's 'blue' meth is the joke.
